wave_0b_performance_reconciliation.downstream_teardown_effect: Client request abort did not cancel the server-side import; teardown raced the still-running handler and could report ENOTEMPTY or leave fixture files.

timing_fixture.lock_wait: Not separately instrumented; sequential single-writer fixture had no competing writer.

wave_0b_performance_reconciliation.correction: ChatStore.saveMany applies the parsed batch under the canonical path lock and commits one validated atomic replacement; FileHandle.sync and old-or-new failure behavior remain enabled.

client_abort_fixture_evidence.observation: The complete imported history existed after the client request timed out, confirming server-side import continued after client abort. Exact-path cleanup was rejected by command policy; fixture remains outside Git under E:\pip_temp.

limits: No cross-process coordination for multiple typed servers sharing a workspace.
No last-known-good backup or automatic recovery from malformed canonical state.
Filesystem failures were injected; no real disk-full event was induced.
Provider batches use one atomic commit; cross-process coordination remains unsupported.
A disconnected provider-import request can continue server-side work; generic cancellation semantics are outside this closure.
